findings.title: Invalid Zod computed property keys in minimumTokenResponseSchema strip expiry and other fields
findings.body: In `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` evaluate `Object.prototype.toString()` on the Zod schema instances at runtime, which produces the literal property key `"[object Object]"` for both entries (with the second overwriting the first). Because `z.object()` strips unknown keys by default, `minimumTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(response)` neither validates that a numeric expiry property exists nor preserves any fields other than `access_token` (stripping `expires_in`, `expiry_date`, `instance_url`, etc.). Callers that read `expires_in` or other properties from `.data` (such as Zoom, Office 365 Calendar, and Salesforce) will receive `undefined`, resulting in `NaN` expiry dates or broken credentials.

findings.title: Saving SafeParseReturnType wrapper instead of `.data` corrupts Google Calendar credentials in DB
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `SafeParseReturnType` object (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed credential data itself. In `GoogleCalendarService`, `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` is passed directly to `prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key } })` instead of `key.data`. This overwrites `credential.key` in the database with `{ success: true, data: { ... } }` on the first token refresh (even when credential syncing is disabled), causing `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` on line 75 to throw a `ZodError` on all subsequent uses of the credential.

findings.title: GoogleCalendarService expects `res.data` but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` object, whereas the fallback callback returns `fetchTokens.res` (a `GaxiosResponse` with a `.data` property). On line 94, `const token = res?.data` evaluates to `undefined` when syncing is enabled, causing `token.access_token` on line 95 to throw a `TypeError` (which is then swallowed in the `catch` block because `message !== "invalid_grant"`, leaving the expired token in place).

findings.title: Missing `prisma` import, missing `refreshOAuthTokens` call, and stale `accessToken` used in SalesforceCalendarService
findings.body:
In `SalesforceCalendarService.getClient`:
1. Line 96 calls `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, but `@calcom/prisma` is not imported in this file, causing a compile error and a runtime `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`.
2. Lines 75-84 call `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` directly instead of wrapping the request in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is never used.
3. Lines 105-106 pass the old `credentialKey.instance_url` and `credentialKey.access_token` to `new jsforce.Connection(...)` instead of the newly refreshed values from `accessTokenParsed.data`.

findings.title: Wrong ID (`credentialId` instead of `userId`) passed to `refreshOAuthTokens` and incompatible `Response` shape in Zoho Bigin
findings.body: In `BiginCalendarService.refreshAccessToken`, line 93 passes `credentialId` (`credential.id`) as the third argument (`userId`) to `refreshOAuthTokens`, which sends the credential primary key as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` instead of `credential.userId`. Additionally, when credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` object rather than an Axios response (`{ data: ... }`), so accessing `tokenInfo.data.error` on line 96 throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')`.

findings.title: HubspotCalendarService treats the Fetch `Response` from `refreshOAuthTokens` as a parsed `HubspotToken`
findings.body: When credential syncing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw Fetch `Response`, whereas the fallback `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)` returns a parsed `TokenResponseIF` object (`{ accessToken, refreshToken, expiresIn }`). Lines 192-202 read `hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn` and `hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken` directly without parsing the response JSON or mapping `access_token`, setting `expiryDate` to `NaN`, saving the raw `Response` object to `credential.key` in the database, and passing `undefined` to `hubspotClient.setAccessToken`.

findings.title: ZohoCrmCalendarService expects an Axios `{ data }` response from `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: In `ZohoCrmCalendarService`, the fallback in `refreshOAuthTokens` uses `axios(...)` which resolves to `{ data: ... }`, whereas `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response` when credential syncing is enabled. Line 217 then accesses `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error')` when syncing is active.

findings.title: Webex `refreshAccessToken` validates synced token responses against full `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` but validates the response using `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse(responseBody)` instead of `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. Because `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` strictly requires `scope`, `token_type`, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`, a minimal response from `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` containing only `access_token` and expiry will always fail validation and reject with `"Invalid refreshed tokens were returned"`.

findings.title: Zoom `VideoApiAdapter` passes directory name `"zoomvideo"` instead of app slug `"zoom"` to `refreshOAuthTokens`
findings.body: Line 92 passes `"zoomvideo"` (the directory name) as `appSlug` to `refreshOAuthTokens`, whereas Zoom's app slug in `prisma.app`, `appStoreMetadata`, and `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts` is `"zoom"` (and `/api/webhook/app-credential` looks up the app by `slug`). This causes `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` to receive inconsistent `appSlug` values between credential creation (`"zoom"`) and token refresh (`"zoomvideo"`).

findings.title: Outbound token refresh request to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` does not send the webhook secret header
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends a `POST` request to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` but includes no authentication headers (such as `[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]: process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`), giving the self-hosted sync endpoint no way to verify that the request for user OAuth tokens originated from Cal.com.
